answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on a shared task result. A grove of new accounts then cannot cheaply manufacture influence: each must tie up real capital, and if colluding agents submit provably false attestations, their deposits are forfeited. Raising a tide of sybils therefore scales the attacker’s cost roughly with voting weight, while honest agents can earn fees without duplicating collateral. A plume of fabricated identities brings no free votes.
